Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a desktop 3D-printing slicer (a fork of OrcaSlicer, C++ with wxWidgets and two React pages; repository `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`, public on GitHub) with its own server in the private tsd-enterprise repository. A person chats with an AI in the app through a JusPrin account, where the server's gateway forwards the chat to an AI provider and charges credits, or with their own key for OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic. They also connect their own printers, save projects, keep a print history, send print reports and buy credits through Chargebee. Over November 2026 the error handling was reworked twice and got it wrong in opposite directions, as the task describes. On 2026-11-24 a real report showed the pattern again: a person's OpenRouter workspace was restricted to their own provider keys, OpenRouter's answer said so in plain words with a link, and the app said "Something went wrong on our side" and filed a report. Kenneth's point was that this failure is one only the person can act on, and that the questions to ask of any failure are common sense: can the person understand it, can they act on it, can we do anything about it, and is it a bug in our code. The error-handling rules were then rewritten around one idea, and he judged that understanding good enough. Three code readers, given only the new text, read the app and the server and produced the list of 42 cases; six were confirmed by a second read, none was run, and no reader reached every file (the gaps are named at the end of the list). The app reports to the developers through `report_unexpected_error` and `report_if_automatic` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`), sent by Sentry's native SDK, and only when the person presses "Report to JusPrin team" or has automatic reports on. The server reports through Sentry's Django integration and the gateway's own top handler. Kenneth wants reports in plain language for a reader who did not see the work: full sentences, no made-up labels, decisions asked as full "Decision needed" paragraphs, proposals marked as proposals, and inference marked as inference.

Task:
Fix the places where JusPrin sends a failure to the wrong one. The list is `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/error-handling-misrouted-failures.md` (an untracked working file; do not commit it): 42 numbered cases in the desktop app and the JusPrin 2 server, each with a file and line.

**Read the rule first.** It is the "Error handling" section of `AGENTS.md` in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (branch `jusprin-dev`) and of `CLAUDE.md` in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (branch `master`). The current text opens with "Someone pastes a key from their own AI service". If the copy you read does not open that way, the new text has not landed on that branch yet: read it in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/error-rules-whose` of each repository, and say so in your first report. Its one idea: a failure has to reach whoever can do something about it, in a form they can use. A failure that is the person's reaches them in words they can understand, true about where the problem lies, with what to do next, and in the other side's own words when those were written for a person; it is not reported. A failure that is ours reaches us with everything the code knew, the person is told only that it is not their fault, and the work stops. A failure nobody here can fix, such as a service the person chose being down, is told to the person truthfully and not reported. When it cannot be told whose a failure is, it comes to us.

**Do not repeat the two earlier mistakes.** JusPrin 2.0.0 told the person "the service could not be reached" for failures that were ours, and nobody heard of them. JusPrin 2.0.1 swung the other way: it told the person "Something went wrong on our side" for failures only they could fix, and filled Sentry with reports nobody could act on. Both came from sorting by code path, status code or a prepared list of cases, not by looking at the failure and asking whose it is. So for each case, read what the other side really says, decide whose it is, and fix the branch for "anything else" so the next unlisted failure of the same kind also goes the right way. Adding one more recognised answer and one more sentence to a list is not a fix. Add no classification tables.

**Questions that are Kenneth's. Ask them at the start, each as a full "Decision needed" paragraph with the options and what each costs, and carry on with what does not depend on them.**
1. How the app shows the other side's own words. One way for every case, for example the service's name followed by its message. He approves that once; after that, showing a service's words needs no approval per case.
2. Every new sentence of ours. Collect them into one list with where each appears, and bring him the list; do not ask one at a time. A sentence of ours needs his yes, quoted in the commit message.
3. The situations the rule does not settle, listed at the end of the working file: whether work that failed must be undone (case 41, a message charged although the AI provider failed); whether a failure retold by the AI model counts as reaching the person; what "the work stops" means for a background save that retries; what the person is told when a report cannot be sent.
4. Case 27 is JusPrin 1's server code. Leave it alone unless he says otherwise.

**Order.** Start with the two cases about money (41 and 42), then the cases a person is most likely to meet. Each group in the working file says which direction the failure goes wrong.

**How to work.**
- Kenneth's rule: never fix what you have not reproduced. Every case in the list comes from reading only, and several are marked inferred. For each, first show the wrong behaviour in the real app or server (a scratch copy of the app with its own data folder, never Kenneth's running JusPrin; the one local server stack that exists, never a second), then fix it, then show the right behaviour. Where a case depends on how an outside service answers, verify that from the service's own documentation or a real answer, not from memory. If a case cannot be made to happen, change nothing for it and say so.
- A failure that is ours gets no handling code: it is thrown where it is found, keeping the other side's status, request id and error text, and the one handler at the top of the entry point reports it. Every failure, whoever it goes to, is also written to the log.
- Send nothing to a real Sentry project. Spend nothing on real AI services without asking Kenneth first.
- JusPrin: new branches from `jusprin-dev` in worktrees under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/`; never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. tsd-enterprise: work in a worktree under its `.claude/worktrees/`, because other sessions share the main checkout; never stage `obico-server` or `.claude/launch.json`.
- New sentences must be translatable and added to the catalogs as the repository's localization rules say.
- Commit only when Kenneth asks, push only when he asks, no attribution lines. Builds on this Mac are shared: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`, build with `-- -j4`, one build per build directory.
- This is a long task. Work through it in groups you can finish and show, and report after each group rather than at the very end.

**Done looks like:** for each of the 42 cases, one of: reproduced, fixed and shown fixed, with a test; shown not to happen, with the evidence, and left unchanged; or waiting on a named decision of Kenneth's. Report in plain language: what the person saw before and sees now, what we received before and receive now, what you tested, and what is still open.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a

Money cases 41 and 42: reproduce, fix, verify

# Failures that go to the wrong one

Found on 2026-11-24 by three code readers who were given only the new error-handling write-up
("a failure has to reach whoever can do something about it, in a form they can use") and asked to
find every place the code does not do that. App code read on `origin/jusprin-dev` (110a9492e0),
server code on `origin/master` of tsd-enterprise. Everything is by reading; nothing was run.
"Checked" marks the cases a second reader confirmed against the code. None of the readers reached
every file; what they did not reach is at the end.

App paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Server paths are under `web_ent/jusprin/`.

## A. Ours, but the person is told it is theirs or the network's, and we never hear of it

App
1. Credits and plans, Billing and usage. `Shell/ServerSheet.cpp:86-97, :215`. A server fault or an ended sign-in shows "Couldn't load Credits and plans. Check your internet connection, then try again." Checked.
2. Email sign-in. `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:314-315`. Any refusal the app has no branch for, and no network, both show "JusPrin couldn't sign you in. Try again." Checked.
3. Password sign-in. `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:312-313`. Any 400 becomes "That password is wrong." without reading the server's code.
4. Delete account. `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:153-159`, `AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:296`. Any failure shows "The account couldn’t be deleted. Check your internet connection, then try again."; status and body are dropped unlogged. Checked.
5. The app's own 120-second limit on a reply, a reply cut mid-stream, or one over 16 MiB. `Agent/AgentTransport.hpp:27-28`, `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:779-782`. Shows "The AI request could not reach the … service." Checked.
6. Print report with no answer (our server down, TLS failure, a large photo timing out). `Home/PrintHistory.cpp:250`, `HomeUI/src/components/PrintReportForm.tsx:139`. Shows "The report couldn't be sent. Check your connection and try again."
7. Update check. `Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp:104-136`, `AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:609`. GitHub answers 403 or 404, or a list the app cannot read: "Couldn't reach GitHub", which is untrue.
8. AI panel will not start. `Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:206, :237-241, :325-332, :372-389`; `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:83-87, :391-394`. Shows "The AI panel could not connect", "The AI page did not complete the bridge handshake." and "Bridge traffic: … sent / … received". Log only.
9. Home will not start. `Home/HomeWebView.cpp:80, 85, 177`. "The packaged Home page is missing from this build.", "The system web view could not be created.", "The Home page failed to load." Log only. The second may be a system part the person must install, and it does not say so.
10. JusPrin model list. `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:51-60`, `AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx:142`. Our server answers a 4xx, or no network: "Signed in · AI unavailable … Try again in a moment." Only a 5xx is reported.
11. Browser sign-in. `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:346-348`, `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:93-104`. Another program holds the port, or our token exchange fails: "Signing in didn't finish. Nothing was saved. Try again." Log only.
12. Autosave. `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:351`, `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:166-185`, `Shell/StatusRow.cpp:430, :615-616`. Disk full, folder not writable, or our bug all show "Couldn't save … JusPrin will retry." The system's reason is dropped, so it cannot be told whose it is.
13. Export, restore, version history. `Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:144-146, :161-168, :184-187`. "The project couldn't be exported. Try again." and two like it; reason logged only.
14. Opening a project. `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:863, 922-954`, `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1446`. Open in a second window, the current project unsaved, or a damaged project: "The project couldn't be opened. Try again." Three owners, one sentence.
15. A saved project that cannot be read gets no card on Home. `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:757`, `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:443`. One cause is permanent: an interrupted chat restore leaves a marker that "requires recovery", and no code recovers it.
16. Projects folder unreadable. `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1017`. "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."; the system's reason is dropped.
17. Profiles shipped with the app fail to install or read. `Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:231, 342`, `PrinterSetup/SetupOptionsLoader.cpp:85`. "JusPrin couldn't load this preset. …" Log only.
18. Save on a proposal card. `AgentUI/src/components/ProposalCard.tsx:31-32`. "The action failed."
19. Tool failures in the app's own work. `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:714-717`. They reach us only with automatic reports on.
20. The local tool server's helper. `Mcp/Bridge/Bridge.cpp:119, 163`. Any failed probe tells the outside AI client "Open JusPrin and a project, then try again.", even while JusPrin is open.
21. Ends in a log line or nothing: the history cleanup warning (`Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:455`); a damaged printer-facts file emptied without a log line (`Workspace/PrinterFactsStore.cpp:56-80`); a kept G-code file that changed (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1246`); a dropped file the page cannot read (`HomeUI/src/App.tsx:218`, `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:311-314`); an unreadable OrcaSlicer.conf read as "no printers" (`Home/OrcaImport.cpp:67`); a print-host test that throws (`PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:895`, inferred); a report that cannot be sent (`Support/SentryClient.cpp:89-93`).

Server
22. The app sends something the server refuses (a field a newer app added, a model removed from the aliases, an empty alias setting). `v2/errors.py:72-76`, `v2/gateway.py:206-211`, `v2/upstream.py:58-131`, `v2/views.py:172-175, 267-270`. Told "The request is not valid." or "This model is not available." We get one log line with the code only.
23. A paid Chargebee event that matches nothing (customer id without the `jusprinv2-` prefix, plan id missing from settings, unknown event). `ledger/billing.py:372-373, 377, 382`, `v2/views.py:104-106`. The credits never appear; silent return or bare 400.
24. Guesses in billing. `ledger/billing.py:154-157`: any Chargebee failure reads as "no card on file". `:168-173`: "subscription not found" on account deletion is taken as nothing to end. `ledger/reports.py:31-32`: any database conflict becomes "This print already has a report."
25. Browser session gone at checkout or on return from paying. `v2/web.py:301-302, 310, 319-321`. A silent redirect to Credits and plans after they paid.
26. Deactivated account or wrong-scope token told "Sign in to JusPrin to continue." (`v2/auth.py:18-22`); deactivated account or lost cache entry told "This link has expired" (`v2/views.py:203-208`).
27. JusPrin 1 code: `jusprin_cb_views.py:105-113` (user not found returns 200, nothing logged), `:168-175` (a bare catch drops the Obico discount), `:60-61` (a cancelled checkout raises a 500), `views.py:67-70`.

## B. The person's, but they are told "Something went wrong on our side" and we get a report

28. Own key: the service names a cause (country, moderation, key spending limit, no access to the model). `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:825-842, :793-796`; key check at `AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx:411`. OpenAI or OpenRouter 403, 404 or 400.
29. Export G-code from Print history to an SD card that is full, locked or unplugged. `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1335`, thrown at `Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder.cpp:454`. A dropped file that cannot be written (`:1496`) and a photo that cannot be read (`:1360`) take the same path.
30. Unreadable attachment (permission denied, drive gone). `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1622-1637`.
31. Sign out with no network. `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:188-193`. Checked.
32. An AI tool exports to a folder that cannot be written. `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:363-411`, `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2690, 2825`. Coded "failed", so it is reported; for 3MF, STL and presets the reason is dropped.
33. Server: a provider refuses the person's own content. `v2/gateway.py:323-330, 352-354`. Inferred; not confirmed which providers answer this way.

## C. Reaches the right one, in a form they cannot use

34. Own key, HTTP 429. `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:751-755, :839-840`. "The OpenAI service is rate limited. Try again shortly."; the service's own words, which may name a daily cap, are dropped.
35. Too large, no next step. `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:757-761`. "The request was too large for the … service." does not say to start a new chat or remove pictures.
36. A Klipper printer's Moonraker answers 401 (key needed), or a proxy answers 502. `Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:70`, sentence at `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:316`. "192.168.1.42:7125 isn't answering." It answered and refused.
37. Printer window. `Home/PrinterWindow.cpp:111, 167-182`. Any web view error that is not a certificate one: "Nothing answered at %s. Check that the printer is turned on…"
38. Server: a renewal's card is declined. `ledger/billing.py:290-294`, `v2/web.py:177-185`. Told "This message needs 1 credit; you have 0." while the page says the plan is renewing.
39. Server: a report photo in HEIC format, or the server failing to read the upload. `v2/views.py:233-239`. One answer for both: "That photo could not be read."

## D. Neither's, but called ours

40. Own key: the service is down or overloaded. `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp` as in 28, in-reply `:501-506`, the model list (`Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:197-201`), and a chat-title request after a good reply (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3491-3506`).

## E. A failure recorded as a success

41. Server: the AI provider fails after the message was charged. `v2/credits.py:55`, `ledger/ledger.py:123`, `v2/gateway.py:191-195`. The person is told "our side" and we get a report, but the charge stands and Billing and usage counts the message. No code gives credits back. Checked. Not checked: whether the app's retry reuses the turn id, which would make the retry free for an hour.
42. Server: a checkout returns "succeeded" with the invoice unpaid. `ledger/billing.py:347-351`. Told "500 credits added" though nothing was granted. Inferred that Chargebee can return this.

## What the write-up could not decide

- Whether work that failed must be undone (case 41).
- Whether a failure retold by the AI model, or handed to an outside AI client, counts as reaching the person (cases 18, 19, 20).
- What "the work stops" means for a background save that retries every few seconds (case 12).
- What the person is told when the report itself cannot be sent, or when they decline to send it.
- Whose failure it is when strangers post rubbish to a public address of the server (`v2/launches.py:34-40` sends it to Sentry).
- A service we chose but cannot change, such as GitHub for the update check (case 7).

## What the readers did not reach

- App: `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, `Agent/ToolResults.cpp`, most of `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` (about 150 of 3,845 lines read), `Canvas/`, `Startup/`, `PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp`, `PrinterCatalog.cpp`, `PrinterDiscovery.cpp`, parts of `HomeUI` and `Mcp/`, and all tests.
- Server: tests, most templates, allauth's own views.

## Error handling

Someone pastes a key from their own AI service, and the service refuses it because of a setting in their account. Only they can change that setting. Later the app loses a chat because of a mistake in our code. Only we can fix that. Every failure is like one of these: there is someone who can do something about it, and error handling is the work of getting the failure to them, in a form they can use.

A failure that is the person's has to reach them in words they can understand, saying truthfully where the problem lies and what to do next. When the other side, meaning the service, printer or system that refused, has already said this in words written for a person, show those words and say who said them, because it knows the situation better than a sentence we prepared. Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing share one sentence, since a second sentence tells them nothing more. Nothing is wrong with the app itself, so it carries on.

A failure that is ours has to reach us with everything the code knew, because we will have to find the cause. The person can do nothing with that detail. They need to know only that the fault is not theirs, and to have a way to send it to us. We write no code to deal with such a failure. Its cause is something we did not understand when we wrote the code, so any handling would be a guess, and a guess carries on in a state nobody can vouch for and hides the failure. The work stops.

Sending a failure to the wrong one is the mistake this section exists to prevent, and it can be made in both directions. Tell the person the service could not be reached when our server failed, and they check their network while we never hear of it. Tell them something went wrong on our side when their own account is out of credits, and they wait for us while our reports fill with things we cannot fix, until the ones we can fix are hard to see.

So look at the failure itself, with what the other side actually said, and work out whose it is. Usually it says. What we have prepared does not change the answer: a failure that is the person's stays theirs when nobody wrote a sentence for it. When it truly cannot be told, it comes to us, because a report we cannot use costs us one look, while a failure of ours that only the person saw is lost.

Sometimes that someone is neither the person nor us. A service the person chose, such as the AI service their own key is for, is down, overloaded or failing on its own side: whoever runs it can fix it, and nobody here can. The person still needs the truth, that the trouble is at that service and not with them or with JusPrin, so they stop looking for something to fix. It is not reported, because a report is for someone who can act on it. Behind a JusPrin account the AI service is ours, because we chose it and can change it, so its failures come to us.

A failure we know people will meet is part of the feature, and the feature is not finished until the person who meets it is told what to do. Every failure is also written to the log, whoever it goes to. The log is where we look when a report or a question sends us looking. It tells nobody anything by itself.

### In practice

- Whose a failure is depends on its cause, such as "out of credits" or "no network", both of them the person's. A status code, an exception type, or the way the failure arrives (an HTTP status, an event inside a reply) is not a cause.
- A branch for "anything else" decides for every failure nobody listed. A failure the other side says is the person's goes to the person, and one that cannot be told comes to us. One sentence there for failures with different owners is a guess.
- A sentence we write for the person needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message. Each has a test, and each time it is shown is counted. Showing the other side's own words needs no sentence of ours.
- A failure that is the person's, or that nobody here can fix, is handled with normal control flow, not exceptions, and is not reported.
- A failure that is ours gets one sentence, "Something went wrong on our side", and a way to report it. Do not sort such failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of one. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- A failure that is ours stops the work and travels up unchanged. Do not catch it, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Once it is clear that it is ours, or that it cannot be told whose it is, turn it into a thrown error on the spot and keep the other side's status, request id and error text.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports through `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`) and tells the person. No other code reports. In the code, a failure that comes to us is called unexpected, and any other is called expected.
- The report carries the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is ours.
- One exception to "the work stops" and "no other code reports": a tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, with no dialog, and for this kind of failure only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- Never record a failure as a success.

### Catching

- Catch a failure only when the code knows what it is and can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against this section. Of each failure the code decides on, with what the other side really says, it asks: whose is it, and does it reach them in a form they can use?

## The design

- **Unexpected errors:** the top handler already logged. Its sister function `report_if_automatic`, used for timers, callbacks and the app-start report, did not. One line in `Support/ErrorReport.cpp` closes that.
- **Expected errors carry what the other side said:**
  - `AgentError` has a new field, `said`. It is filled where the AI service or JusPrin's sign-in answers. It is never sent to the page and never saved.
  - `PrintReportAnswer` has the same field, for the print report.
- **One log line where the person is told:**
  - `AgentHost::told()`: every error sent to the AI page. That covers a failed reply, AI setup, account, outside AI clients, attachments and refused page messages.
  - `HomeHost::told()`: every problem sent to the Home page.
  - The two JusPrin dialog functions. `show_own_error` takes an optional `said`.
  - Each window that shows its own error screen. Each has one line, with the cause passed in:
    - the AI page's connection-error panel;
    - the Home page's error panel;
    - `PrinterWindow::show_problem`;
    - `ServerSheet::set_state(Failed)`.
